policies.sentence: Students must disclose, acknowledge, or cite any use of AI in their work.
Students must describe how, why, and to what extent AI was used, for example by giving the prompt.
Students must name the AI tool used in their disclosure or citation, including its version.
Students must state which parts of their work are AI-generated and which are their own contribution.
Students must include an AI use statement even when no AI was used.
Students are not required to submit a form or note when they did not use AI.
Students need not cite their use of LLMs for writing code, since LLMs are a standard coding tool.
Students must place the AI disclosure in a specified location in their submission, such as a file, README, appendix, or checkbox.
Students must not give false or misleading information about AI use; honest disclosure and self-reporting are relied on.
Students must not present AI-generated or external text as their own without citation.
Students must cite sources and outside help, including AI, as they would cite any other source.
Students must acknowledge AI tools, like other people, as helpers or collaborators.
Students must acknowledge nontrivial help from online forums and AI chatbots.
Students must still attribute AI use that the course permits.
Students cannot receive extension points without an AI usage statement.
The instructor will disclose their own use of generative AI and expects the same from students.
The instructor gives examples of what a proper attribution looks like.
